sourceOccurrences.relationship: Proof with explicit coordinate and stopping conventions
sourceOccurrences.note: A deepest-node removal reduces the difference to a product of two monotone increments.

sourceOccurrences.relationship: Proof with explicit coordinate and stopping conventions
sourceOccurrences.note: Four witness indicators give the conditional comparison without moving an edge between certificates.

sourceOccurrences.label: Stopped-leaf Cauchy–Schwarz
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Proof with explicit coordinate and stopping conventions
sourceOccurrences.note: Independent continuations give an exact leaf sum; adaptive Harris gives the continued-tree version.

sourceOccurrences.label: Stopped DFS witnesses
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Proof with explicit coordinate and stopping conventions
sourceOccurrences.note: Completed branches exclude first entry through them; the ordered attachment points give mixed witnesses.

sourceOccurrences.label: Finite three-point theorem
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Proof with explicit coordinate and stopping conventions
sourceOccurrences.note: Leafwise lower bounds and mixed-witness upper bounds give the factor eight and union estimate.

sourceOccurrences.label: All-but-one DFS witnesses
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2508.18808v1 HTML, Theorem II.3.1 proof, paragraph before (II.3.5)
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Complete proof using the adaptive inequalities
sourceOccurrences.note: A split of the discovery tree at an attachment point gives nonempty marked parts, including endpoint and equal-attachment cases.

sourceOccurrences.label: Higher-order product inequality
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2508.18808v1 HTML, Theorem II.3.1 and its proof, (II.3.4)–(II.3.5) and final display
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Complete proof using the adaptive inequalities
sourceOccurrences.note: Mixed BK and leafwise Cauchy–Schwarz give the stronger coefficient printed at the end of the proof; countable exhaustion is included.

sourceOccurrences.label: Sharpened four-point matching bound
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Complete proof using the adaptive inequalities
sourceOccurrences.note: The smaller higher-order prefactor gives 186624 after applying the three-point bound twice.

sourceOccurrences.label: Three cluster-resampling orders
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2408.08457v1, Lemma 7.1 and Algorithms 3–5; printed pp.11–12/PDF indices10–11
sourceOccurrences.note: Whole-cluster boundaries identify the differences between the shared sets. First entrance into either target cluster gives the path inclusion; complementary independent hybrids give the lower bound.

sourceOccurrences.label: Asymmetric partition inequality
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2408.08457v1, Lemma 1.2, equation (2); section 7.1 proof and (17), printed pp.2,11–12
sourceOccurrences.note: Intersection events, the lower E3 bound and upper E1/E2 bounds give the intended asymmetric inequality. Zero denominators and countable partition convergence are explicit.

sourceOccurrences.label: Quantitative rare-partition implications
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2408.08457v1, Theorem 1.3 and sections 7.2–7.3, printed pp.12–13/PDF indices11–12
sourceOccurrences.note: The product t s squared is at most four times the larger specified split probability. The one-split implication follows separately from the three-point product theorem.

sourceOccurrences.label: Cubic bound on extreme partition probabilities
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2408.08457v1, Section 7.3, cubic polynomial and numerical bound, printed p.13/PDF index12
sourceOccurrences.note: Harmonic means and two explicit monotonicity calculations justify the symmetric relaxation. The bound is not asserted attainable by a percolation model.

sourceOccurrences.label: General adaptive sampling comparison
sourceOccurrences.note: Induction on unassigned coordinates averages the section inequality over independent remaining laws; predictable choices and independent seeds are explicit.

sourceOccurrences.label: Capacity laws and finite-family BK
sourceOccurrences.note: The exact admissible range is capacity-positive probability at most p and capacity-two probability at most p squared. The printed binomial law fails a one-coordinate test; the maximal corrected law proves the finite-family comparison.

sourceOccurrences.label: Coloured configurations and adaptive parity laws
sourceOccurrences.note: Normalized even-parity and full-triple laws give equality for all two-configuration sections and the triple upper comparison for increasing events.

sourceOccurrences.label: Triple mixture comparison
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2408.08457v1, Theorem 8.7, (24); scope of Remark 8.8, printed pp.16–17
sourceOccurrences.note: The four one-coordinate section masses prove the comparison. A two-coordinate example distinguishes product mixtures from mixtures of whole configurations.

sourceOccurrences.label: Common-face exploration and residual path count
sourceOccurrences.note: Recursive rotation order, outermost-path uncrossing, queried dead excursions and replay of every leaf completion; corner and spoke conventions handle repeated face boundaries and edge-disjointness.

sourceOccurrences.label: Planar three-point inequality and finite-family refinement
sourceOccurrences.note: Finite-family adaptive comparison gives the denominator 1+max pair probability. Exact triangle example makes the stopped Cauchy–Schwarz bound strict. Countable extension states its common-face exhaustion hypothesis.

sourceOccurrences.label: Common-face path-count inequalities
sourceOccurrences.note: The k revealed paths are split into n-m and n-l paths, with n-k unshared paths in each completion. Zero cases and finite-witness limits are explicit.

sourceOccurrences.label: Corrected decay consequence with pair distances
sourceOccurrences.note: The product bound is preserved; negative exponents need pair separation for a diameter-only estimate. An exact infinite-line counterexample disproves the printed universal claim.

sourceOccurrences.label: Poisson parameters and the scope of proposed path comparisons
sourceOccurrences.note: Poisson-tail inversion includes zero and infinity, and the binomial route limit is proved with correct path success probabilities. Source conjectures are recorded historically, without a present-status claim.

sourceOccurrences.label: Fair two-exit DFS and the pivot involution
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2408.00978v1, Main theorem; tree and general-maze proofs; Notes on the proof
sourceOccurrences.note: No-cross-edge property and degree-three saturation justify preservation of the full DFS tree. Conditional branching orders are independent fair bits.

sourceOccurrences.label: Several leaf targets
sourceOccurrences.note: Conditional first-target probability is two to minus its reduced-tree branching depth. Three-exit bounds are sharp, and finite dyadic probabilities exclude one third.

sourceOccurrences.label: First exploration direction of an edge
sourceOccurrences.note: Replacing a nonbridge by two pendant targets reduces its first direction to two-exit fairness; bridges have a forced direction.

sourceOccurrences.label: Connectivity-preserving degree reduction and balanced bond search
sourceOccurrences.note: Fixed deterministically open tree gadgets create leaf terminals and maximum degree three before any bond is revealed. Fairness holds for every all-connected configuration.

sourceOccurrences.label: Balanced three-point bound
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2408.00978v1, Application to Gladkov arXiv:2408.08457v1, Remark 6.4
sourceOccurrences.note: Cauchy–Schwarz includes the seed in the transcript. Finite-family adaptive BK retains the intersection subtraction, with zero cases and a countable finite-witness limit.

sourceOccurrences.label: Balanced exploration refinement
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Written proof using the cited maze theorem and a fixed degree reduction
sourceOccurrences.note: TWYR proves the displayed bound and retains an additional finite-family subtraction; the balanced transcript is supplied by04ZU, with degree and terminal hypotheses checked.

sourceOccurrences.label: Conditional three-function identity
sourceOccurrences.note: Exact conditioning identity; the omitted covariance sum is negative for two fair bits and OR indicators. Local one-bit positivity survives; general theorem not disproved.

sourceOccurrences.label: The cone of positive Boolean cumulations
sourceOccurrences.note: Möbius inversion, restriction/difference closure and product closure; increasing OR indicator is outside the cone.

sourceOccurrences.label: Positive formal coordinate elimination
sourceOccurrences.note: Direct multivariate formal-series proof; nonnegative coefficients and local finiteness, including Bernoulli parameters0 and1.

sourceOccurrences.label: Polarization and constant-argument recursion
sourceOccurrences.note: Partition coefficients obtained by formal logarithm/exponential; insertion into blocks gives multiplier n-2.

sourceOccurrences.label: Positive higher correlations for cumulations
sourceOccurrences.note: Every n under a product law; nonnegative Boolean coefficients remain a genuine hypothesis.

sourceOccurrences.label: Failure of coefficientwise monotonicity after elimination
sourceOccurrences.note: The degree-five difference is -1/4; this refutes only intermediate monotonicity closure, not the conjectured final positivity.

sourceOccurrences.label: Three-function correlation on two independent chains
sourceOccurrences.note: Finite-grid minimizer perturbation, product covariance proof, indicator approximation, layer cake and quantile transfer. Bounded nonnegative functions and common monotonicity direction; not arbitrary n or many bond coordinates.

sourceOccurrences.label: Insertion recursion and nested-event formula
sourceOccurrences.note: Cycle insertion proves the recurrence on any probability space; nested events give a1 times the product of j-1-aj.

sourceOccurrences.label: Higher correlations for rectangles
sourceOccurrences.note: Induction in dimension and order, grouping partitions by the block containing a varied coordinate; bounded functions with anchored rectangular level sets follow by layer cake.

sourceOccurrences.label: All orders on the square
sourceOccurrences.note: The simultaneous induction keeps a nonpositive correlation with an arbitrary set disjoint from one decreasing set; grid minimizers then flatten. Includes bounded-function and finite-chain passages.

sourceOccurrences.label: Correlation and formal-series equivalence
sourceOccurrences.note: Formal diagonal expansion and finite coefficient sums; distinct-prime specialization isolates each mixed correlation. The function class explicitly contains zero, permitting unused degrees.

sourceOccurrences.label: Two-bit FKG higher correlations and formal positivity
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Alternative written proof with explicit scope
sourceOccurrences.note: Monotone conditional-quantile sampling from two independent uniforms, including zero and one marginals, transfers L3SC to any two-bit FKG law; I7RH gives formal positivity. This is an alternative proof using the later square theorem.

sourceOccurrences.label: Supercritical separated-mark limit
sourceOccurrences.note: Written proof for translation-invariant independent bonds on Z^d with at most one infinite cluster, fixed k>=2; no rate claimed and ratio requires theta>0.

sourceOccurrences.label: Relative coupling error for rare point connections
sourceOccurrences.note: Elementary probability proposition proved. The percolation coupling and uniform conditional one-arm comparisons remain external inputs.

sourceOccurrences.label: Density factorization and its constant
sourceOccurrences.note: Algebra and gamma identities proved from explicit density hypotheses. Surviving-boundary index correction provisional; source SLE proof remains cited.

sourceOccurrences.label: Discrete triangular-site boundary/bulk factorization
sourceOccurrences.note: Cited theorem, not a wiki proof: two fixed real marks, one fixed point strictly in the upper half-plane, critical triangular-site law. No all-boundary, square-bond or uniform degenerating-geometry extension.

sourceOccurrences.label: Full-plane triangular-site three-point constant
sourceOccurrences.note: Cited theorem, not a wiki proof. Specialized imaginary-DOZZ expression and sqrt(2) open-colour factor checked; fixed distinct macroscopic marks. No square-bond extension.
